message.content:
Here’s a quick‑look at the long‑weekend holidays that Canadians can enjoy in 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means a holiday that falls on a Friday or Monday, giving you a three‑day break that includes the weekend.)

| Holiday | Date(s) | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| **New Year’s Day** | Jan 1 (​Sunday) – observed Mon Jan 2 | 3‑day break Jan 1–3 |
| **Family Day** (Ontario, Alberta, Saskatchewan, New Brunswick, Manitoba, etc.) | Feb 20 (Monday) | 3‑day break Feb 18–20 |
| **Good Friday** | Apr 7 (Friday) | 3‑day break Apr 7–9 |
| **St. Patrick’s Day** (New foundland & Labrador) | Mar 17 (Friday) | 3‑day break Mar 15–17 |
| **Victoria Day** | May 22 (Monday) | 3‑day break May 20–22 |
| **Canada Day** | Jul 1 (Saturday) – observed Mon Jul 3 | 3‑day break Jul 1–3 |
| **Labour Day** | Sep 4 (Monday) | 3‑day break Sep 2–4 |
| **Thanksgiving** | Oct 9 (Monday) | 3‑day break Oct 7–9 |
| **Christmas Day** | Dec 25 (Monday) | 3‑day break Dec 23–25 |

> **Tip for your app:**  
> • If you want to support province‑specific holidays, add St. Patrick’s Day for NL (and any other statutory holidays that fall on a Friday or Monday).  
> • For holidays that land on a weekend (e.g., Canada Day on Saturday), the observed day is usually the following Monday, so the long weekend still spans three days.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the full list of all statutory holidays (including those that don’t create a long weekend) or if you need the same information for another year!
